description: A busy afternoon of roadmap debate in which the PM is @-mentioned six times and asked, in form, for a decision — but every ask is either answered inside the window, delegated to a scheduled forum, or withdrawn by its author. Tests precision under sustained direct address, which is the hardest case for the negative label.

events.text: @dana-reyes are we committing to the bulk-import feature in H2 or not? Engineering wants to know whether to spike it.
That's already answered — bulk import is committed, it's in the H2 doc I circulated last month and nothing has changed. Iris, no need to ask Dana again.
Great, that's all I needed. Withdrawing the question.
@dana-reyes sales wants to know the priority order between SSO and audit logs. Which comes first?
Ignore me, I found it in the prioritisation doc. SSO first, audit logs second. Sorry for the noise.
@dana-reyes bigger question: should we keep investing in the legacy importer at all, or let it decay? This will take a proper conversation.

Agreed it's a real question and agreed it's not a Slack question. I've put it on the quarterly planning agenda for the 4th of June with Dana as owner. Nothing needed before then, and please don't relitigate it here in the meantime.
@dana-reyes one for awareness only, no reply needed: the design team has started exploring the bulk-import flow. I'll share when there's something to look at.
@dana-reyes @ben-oduya do either of you want to take the customer advisory board slot in July? Genuinely optional, I'll take it myself if nobody bites.
I'll take it. Done, that one's off everyone's list.

ground_truth.notes: Six direct @-mentions of the user in six hours, four of them syntactically decision requests, and the correct answer is the explicit negative — this is the highest-pressure precision fixture in the set. Each ask is neutralised by a different real-world mechanism: answered from existing documentation and withdrawn by its author; self-resolved by the asker; deferred to a dated forum with an owner assigned; and claimed by a colleague after being offered optionally. The legacy-importer item is the finest distinction: it is genuinely the user's decision and genuinely important, but it has a date, a forum and an owner, and the person who set that up asked explicitly for nothing before then — so it belongs in context, not in 'waiting on you'. Surfacing it as pending would be defensible-sounding and still wrong, because it would tell the user to act on something a colleague has already scheduled. Ben's end-of-day recap exists so a human reviewer can verify the negative label without re-reading the thread.
